title: Ensure SSE event atomicity and prevent duplicate delimiter replay
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent JSON parse errors in downstream OpenAI-compatible SSE clients when the server emitted partial JSON objects split across TCP frames and when a reconnect/replay path duplicated the SSE blank-line delimiter. Root cause: the emitter and compatibility layer used a naive line-oriented framing that treated any standalone LF/LFCR pair as an event separator without guarding for JSON payloads that include escaped/newline sequences. On reconnect, the replay path could re-emit the trailing blank-line delimiter in addition to the next event's leading 'data:' lines, resulting in an extra empty event or malformed parse in strict clients. This PR fixes reassembly, emitter, and replay logic to guarantee event atomicity and avoid duplicate delimiters. Changes (summary): 1) Implemented a robust SSE reassembly/parser that accumulates 'data:' lines until a true inter-event blank-line is reached, but also treats JSON string contents correctly by not naively splitting on newlines inside reconstructed JSON payloads. 2) Updated the emitter so payload lines are always prefixed with 'data: ' and we guarantee a single terminating blank-line per event; the emitter now escapes a minimal set of sequences and uses a stable boundary on replay. 3) Hardened replay logic: replay no longer re-emits the terminating blank-line from the prior stream; instead, the replay resumes from the next 'data:' token, and the server signals a 'stream-resume' control event when resumption occurs to aid clients that implement deduplication. 4) Added thorough tests: unit tests for the parser with intentionally split frames (embedded newlines, escaped sequences, long lines), integration tests that simulate immediate reconnects and partial write replays, and a fuzz test that runs 1000 randomized split scenarios. 5) Metrics and observability: new counters sse.reassembly_attempts, sse.reassembly_failures, sse.replay_duplicates_detected; emitted log lines include a trace-id for reassembly errors. 6) Backwards compatibility: default behavior is compatible with existing clients; an opt-in config flag openai_compat.sse_strict_mode enables the stricter resume control event for enterprise users wanting explicit resume signaling. Checklist: - [x] Parser implemented and unit-tested - [x] Emitter updated and regression-tested - [x] Replay logic patched and integration-tested - [x] Added metrics and dashboards (grafana panel ids in comments) - [x] Feature-flag gating and rollout plan drafted Testing: see test files (listed below). CI: initial run surfaced a flake8 formatting error in parser test; fixed in follow-up commit and CI passed. Rollout: staged rollout behind feature flag: 0->5% traffic for 48h, monitor sse.reassembly_failures and 2xx stream success; then 100% after stability window. Related: fixes a number of customer-reported incidents (SUP-8731) and should reduce errors in function-calling/tool outputs where clients previously failed to parse streaming structured JSON. Notes for reviewers: pay attention to parser edge cases around JSON strings containing '

' sequences and long-JSON streaming where KV cache dumps occurred in previous incidents. Conventions: emission keeps 'data: ' prefix on every line per SSE spec; control events use 'event:' header (e.g., 'event: stream-resume') and are documented in redwood-openai-compat/README_STREAMING.md.
